dashboard.label: README
dashboard.description: Start here: choose the right WLM Magic Word dashboard and understand its safety boundary.

header.p: Use the playful interface for demonstrations, the search workspace for normal exploration, and the test harness when validating WLM behavior.

article.p: Run SPL with time presets, results, job messages, session history, diagnostics, success toasts, and themed WLM denial overlays.

ul.li: Use it for: day-to-day demos and the complete experience.
Dispatches searches: yes, only the SPL you enter.
Professional mode: keeps feedback inline and suppresses theatrical effects.

article.p: Preview every denial theme, remediation message, color treatment, icon, sound, and the admitted state without needing a real WLM rejection.

ul.li: Use it for: presentations, theme selection, and safe visual checks.
Not for: proving that an admission rule actually fired.

article.p: Uses Splunk's native Simple XML search manager and results table to validate real WLM responses, callback behavior, and repeated dispatches.

ul.li: Use it for: lab validation after Splunk upgrades or detector changes.
Dispatches searches: yes, only the SPL you enter.
Not for: routine searching or broad production access.

ol.li: Preview Pick and review a theme in WLM Magic Word.
Validate Test a scoped admission rule with a dedicated user in Live WLM Test.
Use Demonstrate the complete workflow in Park Search.

section.p: Use | makeresults for the broad DEFAULT test. To test ALLTIME, use a small index-backed search with the time picker set to All time. Use a temporary rule aimed at a dedicated test user, and never generate an expensive search merely to force a rejection.

div.p: Use a dedicated user such as wlm_demo. Do not target an administrator, shared account, or production role.
Go to Settings → Workload Management → Admission Rules and choose Add Admission Rule.
Enter the predicate, choose Filter search, paste the exact user message, select the intended schedule, and enable the rule.
Sign in as the test user, run the harmless test, confirm the matching theme, then disable or delete the temporary rule.

div.code: WLM-DENIED:WILDCARD: Specify one or more explicit indexes.

article.p: Expected overlay: NOT EVERY INDEX! Replace wlm_demo with the exact dedicated lab username.

div.code: WLM-DENIED:ALLTIME: Select a bounded time range.

article.div: Harmless testindex=_internal | head 1 with the time picker set to All time
article.p: Expected overlay: PREHISTORIC RANGE! Prefer a small dedicated test index when available. Do not use | makeresults for this recipe: generating searches are not index-backed and may not expose an event time range to the admission predicate.

div.code: WLM-DENIED: This test search violates the temporary admission rule.

article.p: Expected overlay: AH-AH-AH! This broad rule blocks searches for the dedicated user, so enable it only during the test.

section.p: These themes are available to rules you already operate, but are not presented as portable one-click admission recipes. Concurrency and runtime commonly depend on workload state or monitoring rules; reliable JOIN and real-time identification can vary by version and local policy.

div.code: WLM-DENIED:JOIN: Replace join with stats, lookup, or a narrower subsearch.
WLM-DENIED:CONCURRENCY: The concurrent-search allowance is full.
WLM-DENIED:RUNTIME: Schedule or optimize this long-running search.
WLM-DENIED:REALTIME: Evaluate scheduled or indexed real-time detection.

ul.li: Confirm the predicate resolves only to the dedicated test user.
Put specific recipes ahead of any broader temporary rule, or enable only one recipe at a time.
Copy the marker exactly; the theme name sits between the first and second colon.
Test in Live WLM Test, then demonstrate in Park Search.
Disable or remove the temporary rule and verify the same harmless search is admitted.

section.h2: How a real denial is recognized
section.p: The preferred admission-rule message begins with WLM-DENIED: or a structured theme such as WLM-DENIED:WILDCARD:. The app trusts current-dispatch HTTP failures, SearchManager errors, and job messages. Historical marker text returned as a result value—such as an old event from index=_internal—is treated as data and does not trigger the overlay.
